change: configs/final.yaml unchanged (settings tuned on all of train, incl. holdout)

hypothesis: MS MARCO MiniLM is mismatched to long StackExchange queries and support passages; fine-tuning on train qrels with hard negatives should make the reranker useful on its own and in the interpolation
change: MiniLM fine-tuned on tune_train (774 q, 2808 pos groups, 7 hard negs from hybrid top 200, near-dups of positives dropped, softmax CE, lr 2e-5, bs 4 groups); epoch 1 of 2 and a=0.4 zscore chosen on tune_val (194 q)

hypothesis: domains differ in how much the reranker helps (docs/RERANK.md: MiniLM alone wins in law/monero/quant, loses badly in politics/hsm/genealogy), so a per-domain a should beat one global a
change: per-domain a on top of E1, shrunk toward the global a with strength m chosen by 5-fold CV inside tune_val (m=10 chosen; history a=0.1, economics/travel 0.7, politics 0.6); norm zscore
reason: holdout -0.0043 (CI [-0.012,+0.003]); CV gain inside tune_val was only +0.001. On the original CE the CV picked the global a outright (m=inf)

experiment: three-way RRF of sparse, dense and cross-encoder ranks
hypothesis: rank fusion is robust to the different score scales of sparse, dense and the reranker and may beat linear interpolation with the RRF score
change: replace interpolation with weighted RRF over the reranked top 200: w_s/(k+r_sparse)+w_d/(k+r_dense)+w_ce/(k+r_ce); grid k in {5..100} x weights step 0.1 on tune_val; chosen k=20, w=(0.3,0.3,0.4)
reason: +0.0014 < +0.003. On the interpolation stage alone RRF was below linear interpolation on tune_val (0.3272 vs 0.3304) and on tune with the original CE (0.2837 vs 0.2890)

experiment: reranking depth with the fine-tuned CE (own idea)
hypothesis: a stronger reranker can safely rerank deeper and recover gold from ranks 201-300
change: rerank depth 100 / 200 / 300 with (a, norm) re-tuned per depth on tune_val
reason: tuning kept depth 200: d300 is within 0.001 of d200 on tune_val (rule from docs/RERANK.md: ties go to the cheaper depth), so there was no change to judge on holdout

experiment: re-tune temporal and dedup on top of E1 (own idea)
hypothesis: temporal and dedup were tuned on the old reranker output; with the fine-tuned CE their optimum may have moved
change: temporal grid (boost/fit/fit_years/fit_present) and dedup grid (thresholds x skip 0/1) re-tuned on tune_val: fit_years tau 50 w(2,1,0) center .75 minmax b .5; dedup jaccard>=0.8 skip 0
reason: holdout -0.0068: the large temporal grid overfits 194 tune_val queries (quant 0.314 -> 0.214)

experiment: re-tune fusion k / w_dense with the reranker on top
hypothesis: hybrid_best was tuned for nDCG@10 of the fusion alone; with a reranker on top the best first stage may differ
change: fusion grid k {10,20,40,60} x w_dense {.3..7} on tune_val, interpolation fixed (a .4 zscore); chosen k=10, w_dense=0.4 (was 20 / 0.5). Sparse k1/b not re-tuned (cost: per-domain grid x new CE pairs)
reason: +0.0054 >= +0.003 by the rule, BUT the gain is all iota (2 queries, +0.151); without iota -0.0068, 39 better / 57 worse, CI [-0.009,+0.018]. Kept because the rule was fixed in advance; flagged as likely noise

experiment: fine-tuned bge-small query encoder, frozen doc embeddings (own idea)
hypothesis: the dense retriever was never adapted to these queries; training only the query tower against the cached document vectors adapts it without re-encoding 1.17M documents
change: bge-small query encoder fine-tuned on tune_train (same positives and near-dup-filtered hybrid top-200 negatives as E1, softmax over all negatives, tau .02, lr 1e-5, batch 8); epoch 2 of 3 chosen on tune_val first-stage hybrid nDCG@10 (0.2771 -> 0.3020); used via dense query_model
reason: +0.0060 >= +0.003 (no iota +0.0065, not iota-driven); per-query mixed: 62 better / 68 worse, CI [-0.018,+0.028]; history -0.026. A first run was swap-bound (all doc vectors held in RAM) and was restarted

experiment: extractive query shortening for the first stage
hypothesis: long posts dilute BM25 and the dense vector; title + first sentences + time-expression sentences may retrieve better
change: 34 variants on tune_val, first stage only: first_n {1,2,3,5,all} x time sentences on/off x title x1/x2 x applied to sparse only / sparse+dense; scored by hybrid nDCG@10 and R@200
tune_ndcg@10: hybrid tune_val: full query 0.3020 / R@200 0.7233; best shortened 0.2966 (title x2, whole body, sparse only); first_n=1 variants 0.22-0.24
reason: no variant beats the full query on tune_val (nDCG or R@200), so tuning kept the champion; nothing to judge on holdout. Same direction as RM3 in docs/SPARSE.md: the full post carries the signal

hypothesis: with a 256-token query cap the document often gets only ~250 of 512 tokens; a 128-token query (mostly title + opening) leaves ~380 tokens for the document. Needs a retrain since the CE is fine-tuned
change: same E1 recipe and schedule (2 epochs, epoch chosen on tune_val) with max_query_tokens 128; epoch 1, a=0.35 zscore chosen on tune_val. Other variants (title only, doc windows) not run: each needs a ~30 min retrain and q128 is the one with a mechanism
reason: +0.0074 >= +0.003 (no iota +0.0093); 56 better / 51 worse, CI [-0.012,+0.030]; workplace +0.188 (5 queries) is a large part of it

experiment: ensemble of fine-tuned and original MiniLM cross-encoders (own idea)
hypothesis: the original MS MARCO model and the fine-tuned one make different errors; a three-way interpolation could combine them
change: w_f*z(fusion)+w_ft*z(CE_ft)+w_orig*z(CE_orig) over the top 200, weights on a 0.05 grid tuned on tune_val: (0.3, 0.5, 0.2)
tune_ndcg@10: interp tune_val 0.3430 vs 0.3419; full chain 0.3410 vs 0.3443

experiment: re-tune fusion after the query encoder (own idea)
hypothesis: E5 tuned fusion before the dense query encoder improved (E8); the best dense weight may have moved
change: fusion grid k {10,20,40} x w_dense {.4,.5,.6} on tune_val over E3; chosen k=20, w_dense=0.5 (= the original hybrid_best, i.e. undoing E5)
reason: holdout -0.0068 (CI [-0.020,+0.007]); tune_val and holdout disagree in sign, as in E5 - fusion weights are inside the noise of both sets

experiment: second small dense model (e5-small-v2), small domains only
hypothesis: a second bi-encoder adds recall that the rank fusion can use
change: e5-small-v2 (query:/passage: prefixes, first 512 tokens, fp16) encoded for the 5 small domains only; 3-way first-stage RRF (sparse, bge with E8 query encoder, e5), e5 weight tuned on small-domain tune (w_e5=0.2); first stage only
tune_ndcg@10: small-domain tune first stage 0.3361 vs 0.3276; e5 alone 0.106 vs bge 0.348
reason: full corpus at the measured 170 docs/s = 1.9 h of encoding, plus CE scoring and tuning > 2 h cap, so not run on 13 domains; on the small domains it hurts holdout. e5 embeddings were checked (fp16 = fp32, no NaN): e5 is just weak on these long posts

hypothesis: E3 gained from a shorter query; 64 tokens (mostly the title) leaves ~440 tokens for the document
change: E1 recipe with max_query_tokens 64, 2 epochs, epoch chosen on tune_val
tune_ndcg@10: interp tune_val: epoch1 0.3307, epoch2 0.3309 vs q128 champion 0.3419
reason: both epochs clearly below the q128 champion on tune_val, so tuning kept q128; nothing to judge on holdout. 128 tokens looks like the sweet spot: 64 cuts too much of the question body

experiment: retrain both fine-tuned models on all of tune (own idea)
hypothesis: E1/E3 and E8 trained on 80% of tune; the other 20% (tune_val) was only needed to pick epochs and a, which are now fixed, so 25% more training queries should help
change: CE (q128 recipe, epoch 1 of the 2-epoch schedule) and query encoder (epoch 2) retrained on all 968 tune queries; a=0.35 zscore, fusion and everything else as E3. No tuning
